rights: Generated for VECTOR//NOVA with built-in imagegen; no third-party reference artwork supplied.
usage: Current approved source artwork for cup selection, the trophy cabinet and championship reveals. Four transparent trophies and four opaque backgrounds. Runtime WebP exports and source mappings are recorded in runtime-exports.json.

images.prompt: Create one new standalone trophy icon concept for Founders Cup, the first and easiest championship in VECTOR//NOVA, a premium futuristic anti-gravity racing game. Concept name: IGNITION. A compact, sporty satin-titanium cup with two broad, elegantly swept rising fins cradling a jade-green luminous lens/core in a shallow vessel. The fins suggest acceleration and a starting launch, with a strong asymmetric but balanced silhouette. A short integrated graphite pedestal and a small amount of pearl ceramic detailing. Refined manufactured bevels, purposeful construction, realistic premium product rendering. Muted jade/sage green accent around #85BE99; restrained glow confined to the core and tiny seams, no overbright neon. Make it feel exciting and worthy of earning, with a clear cup/trophy identity, not an ordinary household bowl. As an entry-tier trophy it should use only a few large, clean components and remain much simpler than an intricate orbital-ring trophy or jagged armored crown. Full object visible centered on a square canvas, approximately 10% clear margin on all sides, shallow three-quarter near-front product view, neutral soft studio illumination, crisp sculptural silhouette readable as a game icon at 64–96 pixels. Actual transparent background including gaps within the trophy. No floor, no backdrop, no contact shadow, no environment, no particles, no text, no logos, no typography, no border, no UI, no collage. Exactly one trophy.

Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: a full-bleed abstract cup-button background for VECTOR//NOVA, a premium futuristic racing game.
Input image: the approved purple Apex abstract background is the style and material reference. Make a companion variant: keep its sophisticated low-key lighting, tactile graphite/pigment material, subtle satin sheen, grain, delicately lit edges and fine powder texture, but change the pigment color AND the shape of the gesture as described below. Do not simply hue-shift the original.
Format/composition: one wide approximately 3:1 opaque panorama, the same proportions as the reference. Edge-to-edge artwork. A quiet dark graphite left third with faint material grain leaves room for a separate icon later. The colored gesture lives predominantly in the middle-right and right half. The bottom-middle stays dark enough for a future UI label, but generate no label. No cutout or blank margins. Forms must remain clear when scaled to a small menu button.
Materials: richly textured pigment across smoked graphite, selective satin metallic glints, tactile layered microtexture, restrained dim illumination as if caught under a translucent coating. Mostly matte dark substrate. Keep shadow and pigment detail; no white-hot highlights, loud neon or excessive bloom.
Constraints: ABSTRACT MATERIAL ART ONLY. No environment, landscape, mountains, cliffs, sky, clouds, weather, water scene, planets, galaxy, stars or space scene. No trophy, cup, badge, emblem symbol, logo, crest, shield, wings, foreground icon, text, lettering, number, border, frame, button chrome, UI or contact sheet. No cartoon paint splashes, comic outlines, simple vector shapes, colorful confetti, plastic finish, artificial polygon fragments or literal objects. No purple in the new variant.
Variant: FOUNDERS CUP, the approachable first tier. Use deep jade and soft sage green pigment, with restrained pale-green highlights inspired by #85BE99.
Shape: a broad soft-edged horizontal pigment wash with two gently overlapping rounded sweeps on the right. Delicate feathering, smooth rubbed striations and softly scattered fine powder along its boundaries. An open, calm, spacious gesture that feels welcoming and controlled. Subtle undulations rather than a vortex. Less relief and less density than the purple reference. No aggressive broken edges or sharp bursts. Retain the sophisticated physical texture and selective dim green sheen; the left side is charcoal rather than tinted green. No gold or red accents.

images.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one premium transparent championship TROPHY ICON for VECTOR//NOVA, an original futuristic racing game.
Render one self-contained sculptural award, a physical object on a small integrated pedestal, isolated on genuine transparency. A square canvas, full object visible, centered with approximately 10 percent clear margin. Front three-quarter product view with very shallow perspective, camera only slightly above the object. Neutral studio lighting with controlled crisp edge highlights so the object is readable against a dark menu. High-quality manufactured materials with restrained realistic surface detail. Strong large shapes readable at 64 to 96 pixels; an elegant collectible trophy rather than a cartoon or a logo.
The four concepts deliberately have DIFFERENT silhouettes, materials and levels of intricacy. Follow this individual concept closely. Avoid a generic silver winged trophy with paired swept fins and a central jewel.
Constraints: trophy object only. No scenery, backdrop, floor, cast ground shadow, UI, button, decorative shield behind it, outer badge outline, text, letter, number, caption, watermark, heraldic wing, skull, weapon, logo or contact sheet. No loose particles, smoke or surrounding glow cloud. Genuine transparent background INCLUDING all openings. Deliver one finished standalone square trophy icon.
Concept 2 of 4: FRONTIER — SUNRISE ARC, medium challenge and discovery.
Silhouette: an upright asymmetric sculptural award. A single sweeping brushed-titanium arch rises from the left side of a short chamfered rectangular plinth and curves overhead toward the right, leaving an open gap at the upper right. Inside the open arch, a warm golden half-disc emerges above a thin horizontal silver bar like a sun crossing the horizon. The half-disc is held visibly by the bar and a short understated support. The arch, half-disc, horizon bar and base form four clear large shapes with generous air between them. Taller and more open than a bowl. No conventional cup bowl, mirrored handles, paired wings or towering central spike.
Materials: brushed titanium and champagne-gold metal with a restrained amber enamel inset on the half-disc; soft yellow-gold highlight hue inspired by #E0D08B. Controlled satin reflections, crisp beveled edges, perhaps one quiet stepped edge in the base. Moderate craftsmanship and detail, not intricate mechanical jewelry.
Feeling: optimistic, poised, upward-reaching and adventurous. An elegant step beyond the simple starter cup. The rising sun is an abstract manufactured metal form, not a picture or scenery.

Format: one wide 3:1 opaque image, approximately 2172 by 724 pixels. Edge-to-edge artwork. Premium cinematic sci-fi rendering with convincing detail and restrained, dimly luminous color. Mature and atmospheric, not cartoony. This is a scene with its own identity, not an abstract paint or mineral-pigment swipe.
Composition: the key subject sits slightly right of center and reads clearly at small menu-button size. Keep the left quarter and lower-left darker and visually quieter for a separate icon and title later, but naturally painted. Avoid a harsh black mask. No blank margins.
Constraints: background art alone. No cup, trophy, badge, crest, emblem symbol, wings, icon, UI, border, frame, label, text, letters, numbers, watermark, vehicle, cockpit, character or weapon. No composited foreground graphics. No contact sheet or transparency. Controlled highlights without bright white washout or excessive neon bloom.
User direction: the second cup is yellow-gold, like a sunset beyond the horizon.
Scene: an expansive, tranquil golden sunset across a distant, almost level horizon. The lower half of a large soft gold sun has already slipped below the dark horizon, leaving a narrow luminous crown just right of center. Broad thin layers of haze and delicate stretched clouds catch its last light; gentle amber rays fade upward into a smoked charcoal sky. The foreground is barely suggested as a dark flat atmospheric plane, leaving the image open and spacious. The visual focus is the warm horizon and sun, not mountains, canyons, arches or detailed terrain.
Palette: warm muted yellow-gold, champagne light inspired by #E0D08B, deep amber haze and neutral charcoal shadows. Preserve the yellow-gold identity rather than turning it orange-red. Subtle atmospheric grain and cinematic texture. Elegant, low-contrast depth, softly glowing and quietly epic.

Concept 3 of 4: HORIZON — FORGE CROWN, hard and confrontational.
Silhouette: a tall, heavy, aggressively angular crown-like trophy forged around an open central furnace vessel. Five unequal blackened titanium ribs rise from a dense tapered square pedestal and flare outward, their broken stepped tips defining an irregular jagged crown. Clear large gaps between the ribs reveal a deep crimson inner metal basin. The front two ribs are shorter, exposing the basin, while the rear and side ribs climb higher. Built-up armor collars, nested plates and exposed restrained silver bevels create layered physical depth. Solid, asymmetrical and imposing, with a broad crown above a narrow grounded stem. Not a conventional silver cup with handles, not a sun disc and not orbital rings.
Materials: predominantly gunmetal and blackened titanium with clean satin graphite panels; deep red enamel and low contained red light in the inner basin and a few narrow recessed seams. Red highlights inspired by #DE9191. No purple, green or gold. Metal must remain visibly solid with readable shadow detail; keep red light tightly contained to the object.
Feeling: earned through pressure, heat and danger. More complex and sharply articulated than the first two awards, but only a handful of large legible ribs, not visual clutter. Industrial trophy sculpture, no literal rock terrain, lava waterfall, flames, smoke, skulls or fantasy gemstones.

Concept 4 of 4: APEX — SINGULARITY, the hardest legendary award.
Silhouette: a sophisticated near-spherical orbital sculpture raised above a slim dark hexagonal pedestal. Three interlocking metal gimbal rings on different tilted axes surround a suspended central amethyst-violet lens, like a captured miniature singularity. The outer ring is a broken precision-machined arc; the middle ring is narrower and inclined diagonally; the inner ring frames the dark violet core. Rings have generous open spaces and distinct widths, with small purposeful gimbal pivots, segmented edge inlays and a few open structural braces. The pedestal connects through two subtle asymmetric supports underneath. The lens is dark at its center with a restrained violet rim, never a white glowing sphere.
Materials: satin platinum edges, dark graphite frames, subtle iridescent titanium and finely recessed violet illumination, with amethyst highlights inspired by #B38AE8. Crisp manufactured joints and delicate nested construction make this the most intricate of the four. Keep the overall circular silhouette and three main rings immediately legible; no dozens of hair-thin wires.
Feeling: impossible precision, controlled gravity, otherworldly mastery. This is a luxurious physical science-fiction trophy, not a landscape, star field, magic rune, ordinary bowl, angular mountain peak or paired winged cup. No literal galaxy outside the object. More elaborate and technically extraordinary than the simpler green bowl, gold sunrise arc and red armored crown. Maintain true transparency inside every ring opening.

A dark central throat recedes into near-total blackness, framed by several flowing curved bands of amethyst light and finely textured violet plasma that bend inward and spiral away, giving a clear tunnel-like sense of impossible depth. The surrounding sparse star field is subtly stretched and gravitationally bent near the opening. Soft indigo dust and wispy purple nebular filaments dissolve into the black void toward the left.
